clue.text: We're told sailor's girlfriend may be dressing

indicators.note: signals that the solver should go by how the named character's name is pronounced

parts.note: Olive Oyl is the sweetheart of Popeye the Sailor in the cartoons

explanation.surface: A sailor's sweetheart might be dressed up, or dressing a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor is Popeye; his girlfriend's name, Olive Oyl, is pronounced just like the oil from olives.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from olives is a standard salad dressing, alone or mixed with vinegar.

clue.text: Decay of politician with spin doctor at first

indicators.note: tells us the doctor's letters come at the front of the answer
to spin something round is to turn it so it faces the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A tale of political decline in the age of the spin doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' looks like a single phrase, a PR fixer, but the two words do separate jobs, and 'at first' puts the doctor ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that eats away timber in buildings.

clue.text: Chicks raised wing as indicator of arrival

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means reading them from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a brood is a family of young birds
an ell is an extension or wing of a building

explanation.surface: Young birds lift a wing to signal that something has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BROOD upside down in this down entry, giving DOORB. ELL, a wing added to a building, is mainly an American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing the bell at the front door announces that a visitor has turned up.

clue.text: Lizard, one climbing in South American region

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter climbing moves upward, i.e. towards the start

parts.note: Guiana is the region on South America's northeast coast
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A lizard scales something in a South American region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' takes the I of GUIANA up to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Cover tailored clothing line in clingy material

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so these letters go round the next piece
tailored cloth is cut and refashioned, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailored cover for a range of clothing made from a material that clings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges COVER to VECRO, and 'clothing' wraps that round L. Velcro is one of the trademark names running through the across answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Velcro is the trademarked hook-and-loop fastening fabric whose two faces stick together.

clue.text: Fiddle with stuffing for ravioli noodles

indicators.note: stuffing is the filling inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: Someone tinkering with the filling for a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle with' looks like a verb phrase about tinkering; 'Fiddle' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle is the everyday name for the violin, especially in folk music.

clue.text: Look up and try salacious look

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
to ogle is to look at someone lecherously

explanation.surface: Someone looks up and tries a lecherous stare.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOGLE is a trademark used as a verb, fitting the across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for something on the internet search engine is to look it up online.

clue.text: Caution entering covers of egregious texts

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of another
the covers of a book are its outsides, so take the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a referee books, i.e. formally cautions, a player

explanation.surface: A warning slipped inside the covers of some outrageous writings.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOK, as a footballer is cautioned, goes between E and S, the outer letters of 'egregious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic books are digital texts read on screens or e-readers.

clue.text: Rock star to rest in atmospheric zone

indicators.note: to rock is to shake or unsettle, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a pause is a short rest

explanation.surface: A rock star taking a break somewhere high in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as a musician, but 'Rock' scrambles STAR TO into STRATO.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratopause is the boundary layer at the top of the stratosphere, below the mesosphere.

clue.text: Inhabitant of the White House is a sucker

definitions.meaning: Herbert ..., US president 1929 to 1933, lived in the presidential residence
a ..., a trademark vacuum cleaner, sucks up dust

explanation.surface: A sly dig at a US president as a gullible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' seems to mean a dupe; it is a vacuum cleaner, Hoover being a trademark in the across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover was a US president, and the brand name stands for a vacuum cleaner in Britain.

clue.text: Engineer got a part for car's roof

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or rework it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A mechanic sources a component for the top of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun, the person; it is a verb telling us to rework GOT A PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A targa top is a removable rigid roof panel on a sports car, a Porsche trademark.

clue.text: Writer's life includes reading or writing

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a bio is a short life story
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so either gives R

explanation.surface: An author's life story covers reading and writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Biro is a trademark ballpoint, in keeping with the across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, something you write with.

clue.text: Deal with old currency symbols that are put across here

definitions.text: symbols that are put across here

parts.note: to deal is to trade
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Trading in an obsolete money and the signs on the coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the theme: across answers such as Velcro, Hoover and Biro are trademarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trademarks are registered brand symbols, and this grid's across lights are full of them.

clue.text: Dressing earl, repeatedly endure dressing work

indicators.note: here dressing means covering on both sides, so the doubled word goes round the next piece
the synonym is used twice over

parts.note: to last is to endure
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An earl dresses a wound, enduring it again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the signal to wrap one piece round another.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastoplast is a trademark sticking plaster, a small adhesive wound dressing.

clue.text: Means of painting bridge, covering beam roughly

indicators.note: one piece goes round the outside of the others

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch
a ray is a beam of light
C, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: How to paint a bridge, slapping paint over a girder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' reads as a girder in the bridge picture; it is RAY, a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti artists and decorators apply paint from a pressurised aerosol container.

clue.text: Changing room is icy, star's shivering

indicators.note: to shiver is to shake, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A celebrity shivers in a freezing dressing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing room' suggests a theatre or gym; in a church, it is where the clergy robe.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacristy is the room in a church where clergy put on their vestments.

clue.text: Outspoken Iberian's approval for cafe style

indicators.note: said out loud, so the answer is pronounced like the cry it names

parts.note: olé is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: A frank Spaniard gives a nod to a coffee house's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' seems to mean blunt; here it means pronounced, so the Spanish cry of olé gives oh-lay.
explanation.definitionFit: Café au lait is coffee with milk, so au lait names a way coffee is served.

clue.text: Determined to find no one at home?

definitions.meaning: an ... effort is a wholehearted, resolute one
if everyone has gone out, the whole household is absent

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer literally: every person is out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: All-out describes a full, resolute effort; read literally, every member of the household is away.

clue.text: Boxes for food or water spiked with drug in

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
spiked drinks are tampered with, so these letters are altered in order

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Food boxes, or a drink laced with a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' rearranges the drink's letters to TWARE, and 'in' sets the drug inside. This is another trademark in the across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupperware is a trademark range of plastic containers for storing food.

clue.text: Raised energy, endeavour and turnover, say

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: sap means vigour or energy
a try is an endeavour

explanation.surface: Talk of boosting energy, effort and business turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a business figure; it is a folded pie, an example of pastry, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a folded pastry with a fruit filling, one example of the baked dough.

clue.text: Country club's fashion stop in capital

parts.note: the EU is a club of countries, and the possessive supplies S
ton means fashion or style, as in 'the ton'

explanation.surface: A smart country club fashion boutique in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' suggests golf; it is the EU, a club of nations. EUSTON is a mainline railway station in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a major London railway terminus, a stopping point in the capital.

clue.text: Two officers showing gun

parts.note: the first of the two officers is CO, short for commanding officer
the second officer is LT, short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A pair of officers brandishing a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two officers' works as one phrase: two officer abbreviations, CO and LT, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a trademark revolver, named for its maker Samuel Colt.

clue.text: Musical note fine for reflective pieces

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
E is a musical note
fine as an agreement means yes

explanation.surface: A musical score note praising thoughtful writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective pieces' suggests essays; cat's eyes are the trademark glass studs set into British roads to reflect headlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's eyes are road studs that bounce back car headlights at night.

clue.text: Small child loves snowmobile

parts.note: a kid is a child
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: A little kid who adores a motorised sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski-Doo is a trademark brand of motor sledge for travelling over snow.

clue.text: Rating coat as outdoor covering

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, and a tar is a sailor
a mac is a raincoat

explanation.surface: A sailor's raincoat serves as protection out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outdoor covering' suggests the sailor's raincoat; it is the road surface, Tarmac being a trademark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the trademark road surfacing that covers paths and runways outside.

clue.text: Brief note after sex

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A short message left after a night together.
explanation.walkthrough: Post-it is a trademark sticky note, fitting the across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A Post-it is a small sticky slip of paper for jotting brief messages.
